newsitem.title: UK: Talisman gets OK to develop North Sea Ross field.
newsitem.headline: Talisman gets OK to develop North Sea Ross field.

text.p: Britain's Department of Trade and Industry (DTI) on Thursday gave Canada's Talisman Energy permission to develop its Ross North Sea oil and gas field.
The field, which lies 77 km northeast of St Fergus in Scotland, has estimated recoverable reserves of 66 million barrels of oil and 20 billion cubic feet of gas.
The Ross development, operated by Talisman, comprises two blocks.
Block 13/29a equity is divided between Talisman (50.67 percent), BG Plc (21 percent), Lasmo (16.33 percent) and Clyde Petroleum (12 percent).
Of the second block, 13/28a, Talisman owns 54.75 percent, Clyde 18.92 percent, Lasmo 16.33 percent and Nippon Oil Co 10 percent, the operator said.
A unitization agreement to establish the partners' shares in the Ross development should be completed shortly, a Talisman official said.
Oil from Ross will be exported via a shuttle tanker from a floating production, storage and offloading vessel (FPSO). Gas will be exported via a tie-in to the Frigg pipeline, the DTI said.
The field will be developed by a total of 10 wells and first production is expected in the third quarter of 1998.
Calgary-based Talisman Energy Inc said in April it was bolstering its North Sea activities through the acquisition of BHP Petroleum's 17.5 percent stake in two blocks adjacent to the Clyde field.
It also acquired Kerr-McGee Corp's assets in the North Sea, including an additional 25 percent stake in the Beatrice field and Nigg terminal.
